task.title: Evaluate a chunked path-index format on disk
task.problem: Decoding one JSON string per cached filename can cost more than direct traversal on a warm memory-backed fixture; on-disk benefit is unknown.
task.proposal: Compare v2 JSONL with chunked NUL-delimited paths and direct CAS traversal. Adopt a versioned format only if repeated on-disk measurements justify migration.
acceptance: Compare fresh and warm tool indexes, no index, broad and absent-name queries on large on-disk trees; distinguish tool-cache state from OS page-cache state. Record wall time, search time, index size and RSS.
If adopted, preserve path order and round trips for newline and non-ASCII filenames, detect an unterminated record, and verify atomic publication, concurrent writers and isolation from v2 caches.
evidence: Warm tmpfs 8k-path index, absent basename: 8.5 ms with JSONL vs 3.5 ms with a NUL reader. See https://github.com/rmorozov/bst-utilities/pull/17#pullrequestreview-6013606582 and docs/source-grep-performance.md.
